messages:
sam: Heads-up — nightly perf job shows a regression after switching to the new paged FlashAttention variant (flash_v2_paged). Throughput down ~8-12% for 13B sequences with typical batch mix. nvprof/NSYS snippet below, looks like shared mem bank conflicts spiked and occupancy dropped.

leah: Ugh. Is this the variant that uses the smem-prefetch pipeline? any change to tiling params? :thinking:

sam: Yeah, we flipped to the paged pipeline with tiling=32x8 and pipeline_stages=3 last week. Patch: `serve/runtime/attn: use flash_v2_paged by default for paged models`

miguel: Can you paste the ncu counters? curious about achieved_memory_bandwidth and sm_efficiency. :eyes:

sam: Pastie of trimmed NCU output:

```
== NVPROF SUMMARY ==
GPU Utilization: 78%
Achieved BW: 210 GB/s (peak 320GB/s)
L1 Hit Rate: 42%
SharedMemBankConflicts: 248K
Active Warps/SM: 18 (max 32)
SmOccupancy: 56%
Kernel: flash_v2_paged_attn
Avg Latency per token: +11.4us
```

sam: Compared to baseline flash_v1 tiled config: Achieved BW 290GB/s, bank conflicts ~40K, occupancy ~78%

leah: Bank conflicts that big will kill throughput. pipeline_stages=3 might be causing uneven sharedmem reuse across micro-ops. Did kernel change reorder the reductions?

sam: It looks like the paged variant copies bigger chunks into smem and then strides access with a tile stride that conflicts on our card (A100 MCC?). When we moved to tiling=16x16 occupancy goes up but latency gets worse for long sequences.

jia: Could be a register pressure vs smem tradeoff. flash_v2_paged may use fewer registers but more shared mem per CTA. If shared mem per block exceeds optimal, fewer CTAs -> lower occupancy -> warp sched stalls -> lower achieved BW.

miguel: Try two quick experiments: 1) reduce smem per block by halving tile_k (16x8) and bump blockDim.x to keep warps high; 2) change pipeline_stages=2 to see if fewer staging copies reduces bank conflicts.

sam: Running a quick matrix now. Also toggled KV cache prefetching off for the run (we saw earlier it sometimes causes weird alignment). Current trial: tiling=16x8, stages=2 -> achieved BW 265GB/s, bank conflicts 63K, occupancy 72%, latency -2% vs baseline.

leah: Nice. So there's a sweet spot, seems like the new variant needs smaller tiles on our bin to avoid bank striding. Can we codify a heuristic: if model_size >= 13B and device is A100, prefer tiling<=16 and stages<=2?

jia: Add a quick runtime profiler probe: sample SharedMemPerCTA and ActiveWarps/SM at kernel launch and choose fallback tile/stage pair if Occupancy<65% or BankConflicts>100K. Should be cheap.

sam: I'm prototyping that: added a `kernel_probe` step in kernel selection that runs a 1-iteration microbench with synthetic seq_len=64 to collect counters, then picks the config. Early results: avoids the regression in 95% of workloads.

miguel: Also check batching heuristics: if dynamic batching groups heterogeneous seq lengths, the paged variant's bigger smem spikes could push some batches over the threshold. Maybe prefer flash_v1 for mixed-length batches unless probe passed.

sam: Good call — added a condition: if batch contains >30% short sequences (<32) use flash_v1. That reduces tail latency for those mixes.

infra-bot: deploy: canary of runtime kernel-probe landed on `canary/flash-tile` at 2026-03-10T03:12:00Z :rocket:

leah: Can you push perf numbers to the dashboard? I'd like a per-model regression alert that triggers when median token-us increases >5% after a kernel switch.

sam: Will do. Also saving the profiling traces to s3://redwood-perf/attn/1766010007/ — including ncu exports and the microbench results.

jia: For follow-ups: 1) metricize the probe overhead (should be <1% p99), 2) add fallback to smaller-block flash_v2_paged kernel variant, 3) check other cards (H100) bank conflict behavior.

sam: Yep — plan: finish probe rollout to canary today, run 48h soak, if stable roll to prod next week. Will open a PR with the heuristic matrix.

miguel: Thanks. If you need help automating the NCU parse and alerting, ping me.

sam: Thanks all. I'll post final numbers in the canary thread. :thumbsup:
